title: Lobachevsky's Views of Geometry
summary: Lobachevsky's discovery of Non-Euclidean geometry was a byproduct of his more ambitious plan of reforming the traditional Euclid-style foundations of geometry. This project aligned with d'Alembert's and Condillac's practically-oriented visions of mathematics and aimed at closing the perceived gap between the pure mathematics, on the one hand, and the natural sciences and engineering, on the other hand.
